text:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: gpu-pool 'inference-gpu-usw1' saturated. GPU util 95%, queue depth 620, 429s spiking for request tier=standard. Pager: @Kai (oncall-sre)

Kai (oncall-sre): grabbing it. can someone paste the customer impact? which routes returning 429s?

Support-Bot: hitting multiple customers on /v1/generate and /v1/chat. Recent sample from edge-proxy logs: 
```
2026-03-14T21:02:12Z proxy[router] INFO client=acme-inc route=/v1/generate status=429 reason=token_bucket_exhausted tier=standard
2026-03-14T21:02:18Z proxy[router] INFO client=startup-co route=/v1/chat status=429 reason=rate_limit tier=standard
```

Jamie (SRE): autoscaler didn't add nodes. pool shows scale_limit=8, current=8, desired=18 but capped. queue-growth alarm triggered at ~18:58 UTC.

Luis (ML infra): confirmed. sampler from runtime: 
```
$ rwdctl pool show inference-gpu-usw1 --json
{"name":"inference-gpu-usw1","region":"us-west1","current_nodes":8,"max_nodes":8,"desired_nodes":18,"gpu_util":0.95,"queue_depth":620}
```

Kai (oncall-sre): why is max_nodes 8? that should be 32 for this pool normally. did a policy change land?

Luis (ML infra): quick check — looks like a deploy of autoscaler-policy for cost-control rolled an updated tier cap this morning. policy id: restrict-0314. It reduced pool max_nodes to 8 for non-dedicated pools.

Ana (Product): that restricts traffic for many PLG customers — we need to prioritize enterprise SLAs. who gets impacted?

Support-Bot: affected customers: acme-inc (enterprise), devtools-io (standard), free-tier experiments. enterprise traffic seeing higher error rates but we have retries for some SDKs.

Jamie (SRE): immediate mitigations:
1) raise pool max_nodes to 20 (temporary)
2) patch token-bucket refill for standard tier to reduce 429s until scale catches up
3) route high-value enterprise traffic to fallback model variant that runs on dedicated pool (lower qps but not rate-limited)

Kai (oncall-sre): doing 1 now. 
```
$ rwdctl pool update inference-gpu-usw1 --max-nodes 20
Applied policy: max_nodes=20
```

system: pool update succeeded, new max_nodes=20.

Jamie (SRE): starting 2 — token bucket tweak. current policy: 
```
policy tier=standard token_bucket_rate=50 token_bucket_burst=200
```
We propose bump to rate=200 burst=800 for 10 minutes. that will reduce 429s at cost of short-term token surge.

Luis (ML infra): applying change to edge rate-limiter config now.
```
$ rwdctl rate-limiter set --tier standard --rate 200 --burst 800 --expires 10m
OK
```

Support-Bot: observed 429 rate dropping ~45s after change. sample logs: 
```
2026-03-14T21:05:02Z proxy[router] INFO client=acme-inc route=/v1/generate status=200 latency=0.21s
2026-03-14T21:05:12Z proxy[router] WARN tier=standard 429_rate=0.12 -> 0.02
```

Ana (Product): routing enterprise customers to fallback. who's on infra to update routing policy?

Luis (ML infra): I'll add a quick route rule for enterprise org ids to use dedicated-infer-usw1 fallback-model:quantized-v1.
```
$ rwdctl routing add --org acme-inc --route /v1/* --model dedicated-infer-usw1:quantized-v1 --priority high
Applied
```

Jamie (SRE): autoscaler now observing desired_nodes dropping from 18 to 12 as queue clears; new nodes provisioning. 

Kai (oncall-sre): are we seeing residual errors or any stuck requests in prefix cache?

Luis (ML infra): prefix cache healthy. some SDKs were retrying aggressively causing bursts — I'm asking Growth to throttle client SDK retry jitter.

Support-Bot: customer-facing incident note queued to write: "We're investigating elevated 429s on inference routes in us-west1; mitigation in progress." Ana can you own comms?

Ana (Product): yes, drafting status update. Will call out impacted orgs and instruction to contact SEs for high-priority routing.

Jamie (SRE): action items before handoff:
- Revert restrict-0314 policy or scope it to non-production pools (Luis)
- Postmortem to capture root cause: policy rollout lacked canary and increased cost constraints without traffic-aware guardrails (Kai/Jamie)
- SDK retry policy changes and guidance (Growth/Client SDK teams)
- Confirm long-term capacity increases or new autoscaler guardrails (Infra + SRE)

Luis (ML infra): I will rollback the policy to original limits and add an explicit canary. running: 
```
$ rwdctl policy rollback restrict-0314 --to-revision 1
OK — policy reverted. max_nodes back to 32 for inference-gpu-usw1
```

system: pool max_nodes=32, autoscaler reconciling. queue depth down to 40, gpu_util 0.62. 429 rate near baseline.

Kai (oncall-sre): thanks team. marking incident as mitigated. leaving postmortem request in #postmortems and assigning to Jamie/Luis. I'm handing off to night oncall @Selina — please review the postmortem draft and continue follow-ups.

Selina (night-oncall) (automated note): acknowledged handoff from Kai. monitoring alerts: queue-growth cleared, rate-limiter changes expire in 7m.

Ana (Product): status update posted to customers. linking internal hunting doc.

Jamie (SRE): quick timeline note to include in postmortem:
- 21:02 UTC alert — queue growth and 429 spike
- 21:03 oncall paged to Kai
- 21:04 identified restrict-0314 as cause
- 21:05 increased token-bucket to 200/800 (10m)
- 21:06 raised pool max_nodes to 20, applied routing for enterprise
- 21:09 policy rollback started -> restored max_nodes=32
- 21:14 queue stabilized, incident mitigated

Support-Bot: incident severity: Sev2 (customer-facing but mitigated within 15m).

Kai (oncall-sre): closing pager. follow-ups in epic INFRA-1583 (autoscaler guardrails) and PM ticket for customer communication audit. Good job. :thumbsup:

(Reaction: :thumbsup: added by Ana)
